bills.t: Elimination of Rabies and Registration of Dogs
bills.about: Rabies vaccination, dog registration and breeding licences.

impl.sum: Makes yearly rabies vaccination and registration compulsory for dogs, run by local authorities.

figs.l: penalty if still unregistered after 14 days
maximum fine, e.g. abandoning a dog
maximum jail for abandoning a dog

changes: Dogs over six weeks old must be vaccinated and registered every year with the local authority.
Local authorities keep a Register of Dogs, vaccinate stray dogs, and sterilise and release them where they were caught.
Breeding dogs for sale needs a local authority licence, renewed every 12 months.
A dog confirmed rabid may be put down by a government vet; healthy detained dogs are vaccinated, sterilised and released.
Owners are liable for damage their dogs cause.
Replaces the Rabies Ordinance and the Dog Registration Ordinance.
impl.when: The bill sets no start date.
impl.note: Based on the bill as presented on 24 September 2026. Parliament may amend it before it passes.

bills.t: Poisons, Opium and Dangerous Drugs (Amendment), Bill 79
bills.about: How seized drugs are recorded, tested and destroyed.

impl.sum: Lets seized drugs be destroyed before a trial ends, keeping a sample, and sets deadlines for laboratory reports.

figs.l: maximum wait for a destruction hearing
to destroy drugs after the order

changes: Investigators must photograph, and where possible video, seized drugs and report the quantity to the Magistrate.
Seized drugs are destroyed on a Magistrate's order; for cannabis, only a sample goes to the Government Analyst.
A Magistrate's destruction order is final and cannot be challenged in any court.
Retained samples are destroyed when the trial ends.
Police, customs and excise officers all count as investigators.
impl.when: The bill sets no start date. It becomes law when the Speaker signs the certificate.
impl.note: Passed with amendments on 22 October 2026. Based on the bill as presented; the final Act text is awaited.

bills.t: Poisons, Opium and Dangerous Drugs (Amendment), Bill 80
bills.about: Methamphetamine offences, a new manufacturing offence and tighter bail.

impl.sum: Treats methamphetamine like heroin and cocaine, adds a manufacturing offence and restricts bail in large cases.

figs.l: jail for the new manufacturing offence
pure quantity that triggers the bail rule

changes: Methamphetamine joins heroin, cocaine, morphine and opium in the most serious drug offences (section 54A).
New offence of manufacturing other dangerous drugs in Groups A to E, tried in the High Court without a jury.
Manufacturing methamphetamine on the high seas becomes an offence.
Where 100 g or more is involved and the offence carries death or life imprisonment, only the Court of Appeal can grant bail, in exceptional circumstances.
Cannabis sativa and its preparations are listed as dangerous drugs.
who: High Court and Court of Appeal
impl.when: The bill sets no start date. It becomes law when the Speaker signs the certificate.
impl.note: Passed with amendments on 22 October 2026. Based on the bill as presented; the final Act text is awaited.

bills.about: The 2027 Budget: government spending and borrowing for the year.

impl.sum: Authorises Rs. 4,992.8 billion of spending in 2027 and caps outstanding borrowing at Rs. 3,800 billion.
changes: Sets the spending limit for every ministry, department and provincial council for 2027.
Caps the outstanding balance of government borrowing under the Act at Rs. 3,800 billion.
Separately estimates Rs. 4,927.2 billion charged directly on the Consolidated Fund.
Sets limits for advance accounts, which can be varied only with Parliament's approval.
impl.when: Covers 1 January to 31 December 2027. Final vote on 14 December 2026.
impl.note: Figures from the bill as presented on 7 October. They can change at committee stage.

bills.about: A single law for entry, exit, visas and travel documents.

impl.sum: Would replace the 1948 immigration law and the 1971 passport law with one Act.

figs.l: jail for breaching a prohibition order

changes: Repeals the Immigrants and Emigrants Act and the Passport (Regulation) and Exit Permit Act of 1971.
Allows short visits without a visa through travel authorisation set by Gazette order.
Everyone leaving Sri Lanka, citizens included, must allow identifying information to be captured.
False information in a visa application: up to a year in prison, a fine up to Rs. 100,000, or both.
impl.note: Bill as presented on 7 October 2026. A Supreme Court petition was announced on 21 October.

bills.about: Gives effect to the UN Convention against Transnational Organized Crime.
Gives effect to UN Security Council Resolution 2178 of 2014.
Amends the Trusts Ordinance (Chapter 87).
Bill on Sri Lanka Cricket. Under Supreme Court review.

bills.t: Protection of the State from Terrorism
bills.about: Under Supreme Court review after petitions announced from 7 October.
Amends the Civil Procedure Code.
Amends the law on community-based corrections.
Asset declarations, penalties and bail under the 2023 anti-corruption law.

impl.sum: Widens who must declare assets, raises state-ownership thresholds to 50% and sets penalties of at least three times corrupt gains.

figs.l: minimum penalty on corrupt gains or losses
union members before leaders must declare

changes: More people must declare assets, including staff officers of statutory bodies, media company proprietors and editors, and registered sports bodies.
Election candidates file a copy of their declaration with the Commissioner of Elections alongside nomination papers.
Courts must order a penalty of at least three times the corrupt gain or the loss caused to the Government.
Public official and scheduled institution definitions now apply where the State holds 50% or more, not 25%.
The Commission can look into conflicts of interest as well as illicit enrichment.
An information officer under the Right to Information Act must be appointed within three months.
impl.when: Certified 19 October 2026. The Act sets no separate start date.
impl.note: Passed with amendments on 8 October. The bail limits and the offence for misusing a redacted declaration in the bill do not appear in the Act.

bills.about: Who runs export agriculture and which crops count.

impl.sum: Upgrades the Department's top posts and narrows which crops count as export agricultural crops.
changes: The head of the Department becomes Director General, with Additional Director Generals and Directors.
An export agricultural crop is now a crop with export potential that the Minister has notified.
Paddy, vegetables, fruits, root crops, other food crops and plantation crops are excluded.
who: Growers and exporters of notified crops
impl.when: Certified 6 October 2026; published 9 October.

bills.about: Judges' retirement ages and the size of the Court of Appeal.

impl.sum: Raises judges' retirement ages, limits a Chief Justice to six years and allows a larger Court of Appeal.

figs.l: Court of Appeal judges besides its President (was 19)

changes: Supreme Court judges retire at 67 and Court of Appeal judges at 65.
A Chief Justice retires at 67 or after six years in the post, whichever comes first; the serving Chief Justice is exempt.
The Court of Appeal can have up to 24 judges besides its President, up from 19.
impl.when: Certified 25 September 2026.

bills.about: More judges and new retirement ages.

impl.sum: Raises the cap on judges from 110 to 120 and sets retirement ages for other judges and magistrates.

figs.l: retirement age for other judges and magistrates

changes: Section 4(a) of the Judicature Act: up to 120 judges, from 110.
An age limit in section 6(3) rises from 61 to 63.
All other judges and magistrates retire at 62.
impl.when: Certified 25 September 2026.

bills.about: Abolishes the office of Chief of Defence Staff.

impl.sum: Abolishes the office of Chief of Defence Staff, created by law in 2009.

figs.l: year the office was created by law

changes: Repeals the Chief of Defence Staff Act, No. 35 of 2009.
The office ceases to exist; its property passes to the Ministry of Defence.
impl.when: Passed 9 September without a division; certified 22 September 2026.

bills.t: Employment of Women, Young Persons and Children (Amendment)
bills.about: Higher fines under the 1956 employment law.

impl.sum: Raises fines under three sections of the 1956 law from Rs. 10,000 to Rs. 100,000.
changes: Sections 7, 13 and 20A of Act No. 47 of 1956: fines rise from Rs. 10,000 to Rs. 100,000.
Applies only to offences committed after the Act comes into operation.
impl.when: Certified 8 September 2026; published 11 September.

bills.t: Convention on the Suppression of Terrorist Financing (Amendment)
bills.about: Terrorist financing, foreign fighters, virtual assets and asset freezes.

impl.sum: Extends terrorist-financing offences to foreign fighters and virtual assets, with longer asset freezes.
changes: Financing the travel, recruitment or transport of foreign terrorist fighters is an offence.
Virtual assets count as funds and property.
Prosecutors need not prove the funds were used in a specific attack.
Police may use surveillance, undercover work and computer access, some only with court orders.
Covers acts abroad aimed at Sri Lanka, its citizens or government facilities.
impl.when: Certified 4 August 2026; published 7 August.

bills.about: Anti-money-laundering duties for banks and other businesses.

impl.sum: Extends anti-money-laundering duties to more businesses and raises administrative penalties to Rs. 100 million.

figs.l: working days to report a suspicion

changes: Covers designated non-financial businesses: gambling, real estate agents, dealers in precious metals and stones, and some lawyers, notaries and accountants.
Risk-based customer checks, including identifying beneficial owners.
Suspicious transactions must be reported within two working days.
The Financial Intelligence Unit sits within the Central Bank and is operationally independent.
Undeclared cash at the border: a fine up to three times the amount, up to a year in prison, or both.
impl.when: Passed 9 July; certified 4 August 2026.
impl.note: Based on the bill as presented on 9 April 2026; the certified Act may differ.

bills.about: Which animals the Animals Act covers.

impl.sum: Two parts of the Animals Act now also cover goats, pigs and sheep, and one also covers poultry.
changes: Part II now covers goats, pigs and sheep as well as cattle and buffalo.
Part IV covers sheep, goats, pigs and poultry as well as cattle and buffalo.
impl.when: Certified 18 August 2026; published 21 August.

bills.t: National Water Supply and Drainage Board (Amendment)
bills.about: Powers and charges of the National Water Supply and Drainage Board.

impl.sum: Lets the Water Board take over local water schemes, charge sewerage by discharge and set up subsidiaries.
changes: The Board can take over water or sewerage schemes run by local authorities, industrial estates and parks, and community organisations.
Sewerage charges are based on total discharge, whatever the source of the water.
The Board can set up subsidiaries and sell laboratory, training and consultancy services.
The Board can recover the value of wasted water on top of any fine.
Bills and notices can be sent electronically.
impl.when: Certified 18 August 2026; published 21 August.

bills.about: Widens money laundering offences and raises fines under the 2006 Act.

impl.sum: Widens money laundering offences, covers acts abroad and raises several fines tenfold or more.

figs.l: maximum jail in one section, was 1

changes: Using, buying, transferring or acquiring beneficial ownership of criminal proceeds, or property converted from them, is an offence.
Covers acts committed wholly or partly outside Sri Lanka.
Facilitating or counselling others in money laundering is an offence.
The minimum five-year jail term is removed; the court sets the period.
Fines rise, for example from Rs. 50,000 to Rs. 500,000 in section 5.
impl.when: The Act sets no start date. Certified 4 August 2026.

bills.about: A smaller Central Environmental Authority board and changes to the 1980 environment law.

impl.sum: Reconstitutes the Central Environmental Authority as a five-member body with environmental experts.
changes: The Authority has one ex officio Additional Secretary and four members appointed by the President.
Three appointed members need at least ten years of environmental management expertise.
Some officer posts in section 7 must be at least Senior Assistant Secretary rank.
impl.when: The Act sets no start date. Certified 21 July 2026.

bills.about: Moves VAT on foreign digital services to July 2026 and raises VAT on financial services.

impl.sum: Starts VAT on foreign digital services from July 2026 and raises VAT on financial services to 20.5%.

figs.l: VAT on foreign digital services begins

changes: Non-resident digital service providers register when sales to Sri Lanka pass Rs. 60 million a year or Rs. 15 million a quarter.
A customer counts as in Sri Lanka if two signs point there, such as address, bank, card or IP address.
VAT on financial services rises from 18% to 20.5% for periods from 1 July 2026.
Services by registered garment buying offices to overseas buyers, paid in foreign currency, are zero-rated from October 2025.
Entertainment tax is deducted from the value of film ticket sales.
impl.when: Certified 30 June 2026. Main changes apply from 1 July 2026.

bills.about: A new law on mediating civil and commercial disputes, replacing the 2000 commercial mediation law.

impl.sum: Sets out how civil and commercial disputes are mediated by agreement, by choice or on a court's referral.

figs.l: year of the commercial mediation law repealed

changes: Applies to mediation under an agreement, by voluntary referral or on referral by a court.
Parties can agree to mediation by a contract clause or a separate written agreement.
Disputes that need a court decree to settle cannot be mediated, though related matters can.
Mediation Boards and special-category mediation stay under their own laws.
Repeals the Commercial Mediation Centre of Sri Lanka Act, No. 44 of 2000.
impl.when: The Act sets no start date. Certified 30 June 2026.

bills.t: Rescue, Rehabilitation and Insolvency (Corporate and Personal)
bills.about: A new insolvency code for companies and individuals, with an Insolvency Regulatory Authority.

impl.sum: Replaces the old insolvency laws with one code for rescuing viable businesses and handling personal and corporate insolvency.

figs.l: after certification before most provisions start
maximum delay the Minister can add
debt level in several personal procedures

changes: Creates an Insolvency Regulatory Authority and an Official Receiver, and registers insolvency practitioners.
Sets procedures for personal insolvency, including a debt protection moratorium and debt restructuring arrangements.
Provides rescue and rehabilitation routes for viable businesses, including small and medium enterprises.
Repeals the Insolvency Ordinance and several Parts of the Companies Act.
impl.when: Six months after certification on 17 June 2026, unless the Minister extends it.

bills.about: Wide changes to income tax rules, rates and allowances, several backdated.

impl.sum: Amends many income tax rules, raises several 10% rates and adds a 100% allowance for new investment.

figs.l: capital allowance for qualifying new undertakings
cap on head office expense deduction

changes: Five 10% rates in the First Schedule rise to 15% or 30% from the date the Act was certified.
Gains from selling motor vehicles count as income from other sources.
New undertakings investing US$ 250,000 to US$ 3 million in depreciable assets get a 100% capital allowance.
Head office expenses are deductible up to 10% of assessable income from the business.
Gifts of assets to the Government or a university are treated as made at cost.
impl.when: Certified 3 June 2026. Many provisions are dated from 2018 to April 2026 in a table in the Act.

bills.about: Lowers the registration threshold for the levy and extends it to motor vehicles.

impl.sum: From July 2026, businesses must register for the levy at Rs. 36 million yearly turnover; motor vehicles join in May.
changes: From 1 July 2026, register within 15 days once quarterly turnover passes Rs. 9 million or yearly turnover passes Rs. 36 million.
Deregistration is possible where four-quarter turnover stays at or below Rs. 36 million.
An import item in Part IA ends for imports from 1 May 2026.
Motor vehicles are added to Part IB from 1 May 2026.
impl.when: Certified 9 April 2026. Dated changes apply from 1 May and 1 July 2026.

bills.about: A regulator for moneylending and microfinance businesses, replacing the 2016 Microfinance Act.
High Court jurisdiction over drug offences committed on the high seas.

impl.sum: Gives the High Court jurisdiction over drug offences on the high seas, as well as piracy.
changes: Section 9 of the Judicature Act now covers offences on the high seas under the drugs Ordinance and the 2008 narcotics conventions Act.
Piracy under the law of nations stays covered.
The Sinhala text prevails if the Sinhala and Tamil texts differ.
who: People accused of drug offences at sea
impl.when: The Act sets no start date. Certified 6 March 2026.

bills.about: New offences for making or trafficking drugs on the high seas.

impl.sum: Makes manufacturing, possessing or trafficking drugs on the high seas an offence, with stateless ships forfeited.

figs.l: for making heroin or cocaine at sea

changes: New section 54AA covers Sri Lankan-registered and stateless ships on the high seas, whatever the offender's nationality.
Manufacturing heroin, cocaine, morphine or opium there carries death or life imprisonment.
Possessing or trafficking listed drugs above set amounts carries penalties set in a schedule.
Stateless ships used in such offences can be forfeited.
who: People accused of drug offences at sea
impl.when: The Act sets no start date. Certified 6 March 2026.

bills.t: Institute of Real Estate Professionals, Sri Lanka
bills.about: Sets up a professional institute to register and discipline real estate professionals.

impl.sum: Creates an institute to register real estate professionals and keep professional standards and discipline.
changes: Establishes the Institute of Real Estate Professionals, Sri Lanka.
It enrols and registers members.
It maintains professional standards and discipline.
It protects the public interest in relation to the real estate profession.
impl.when: The Act sets no start date. Certified 19 February 2026.

bills.about: Repeals the 1977 law on pensions for former Members of Parliament.

impl.sum: Repeals the Parliamentary Pensions Law of 1977; pensions paid under it stop.
changes: Repeals the Parliamentary Pensions Law, No. 1 of 1977.
People receiving a pension under that Law, or under section 9 of Acts No. 1 of 1982 and No. 47 of 1990, stop receiving it.
Pensions under the repealed provisions stop from the date the Act comes into operation.
who: Former Members of Parliament receiving pensions
impl.when: The Act sets no start date. Certified 17 February 2026.

bills.t: Licensing of Shipping Agents, Freight Forwarders, Non-Vessel Operating Common Carriers and Container Operators (Amendment)
bills.about: Moves container operator licensing to the new Container Depot Operators Act.

impl.sum: Removes container operators from the 1972 shipping licensing law; their licences move to Act No. 3 of 2026.
changes: The 1972 Act is renamed without the words Container Operators.
The definition of container operators is removed.
Pending container operator applications are treated as made under the Licensing of Container Depot Operators Act.
Existing container operator licences continue under that Act.
impl.when: The Act sets no start date. Certified 17 February 2026.

bills.about: A licence from the Director-General of Merchant Shipping to run a container depot.

impl.sum: Only licensed companies may run container depots, under licences issued by the Director-General of Merchant Shipping.
changes: Running a container depot business needs a licence from the Director-General of Merchant Shipping.
Only companies incorporated under the Companies Act may apply.
Applications with false or misleading information are rejected.
Licences cannot be transferred, and terms can change after a chance to show cause.
Monopolising container depot operations is an offence.
impl.when: The Act sets no start date. Certified 17 February 2026.

bills.about: Who can be elected Dean of a Faculty or Head of Department, and term limits.

impl.sum: Widens who can be elected Dean and limits Deans to two terms.
changes: The Faculty Board elects the Dean from its Senior Professors, Professors, Associate Professors and Senior Lecturers (Grade I).
A Head of Department elected Dean gives up the headship.
A Dean can be removed only by the Council under procedure set by the Commission.
Section 51 on Heads of Departments is replaced.
impl.when: The Act sets no start date. Certified 3 February 2026.

bills.about: Shorter tax holidays and cost-benefit checks for strategic development projects.

impl.sum: Caps strategic project exemptions at ten years and requires Finance Ministry cost-benefit analysis and public monitoring reports.
changes: Exemptions for a Strategic Development Project last at most ten years instead of 25.
The Board of Investment identifies projects against prescribed criteria.
The Ministry of Finance does an ex-ante cost-benefit analysis within one month.
The Board monitors projects afterwards and the Ministry publishes outcomes and fiscal impacts online.
Projects missing agreed targets can lose concessions or pay penalties after a chance to show cause.
impl.when: The Act sets no start date. Certified 17 December 2025.

bills.about: Raises the betting and gaming levy rate to 18% from January 2026.

impl.sum: Raises the levy rate to 18% from 2026 and doubles a levy set in US dollars.
changes: The 15% rate under subsection (1A)(c) applies only until 31 December 2025.
From 1 January 2026 the rate is 18%.
The amount in subsection (1AA)(b) rises from US$ 50 to US$ 100.
impl.when: Certified 17 December 2025. The higher rate applies to years starting on or after 1 January 2026.

bills.about: Changes which electricity, fuel, port and financial services the levy covers.

impl.sum: Adjusts the levy's exemption lists for electricity, fuel, container terminals and financial services.

figs.l: VAT rate on financial services named

changes: The Ceylon Electricity Board item applies only to supplies before 18 February 2025.
The fuel item is reworded for sales from 1 July 2025.
Services by container terminal operators for international transport are added to a Part II item.
Financial services already liable to VAT at 20.5% are added as a new item.
impl.when: Certified 17 December 2025. Two changes are treated as in force from 18 February 2025 and 1 July 2025.

bills.about: The 2026 Budget: government spending and borrowing for the year.

impl.sum: Authorises Rs. 4,434.4 billion of spending in 2026 and caps borrowing at Rs. 3,740 billion.
changes: Sets spending for every ministry and department for 2026.
Limits loans raised during or outstanding at the end of 2026 to Rs. 3,740 billion.
Sets limits for advance account activities.
Loan details go in the final budget position report to Parliament.
impl.when: Covers 1 January to 31 December 2026.

bills.about: Changes start dates and request deadlines under the 2022 data protection law.

impl.sum: Lets the Minister set start dates by Gazette and gives controllers one month to answer data requests.

figs.l: to answer a data subject's request

changes: The rest of the 2022 Act starts on dates the Minister sets by Gazette order.
Controllers must say within one month whether a request is granted or refused, with reasons.
The deadline can be extended by two months if the data subject is told in time.
Controllers must tell data subjects they can appeal a refusal to the Data Protection Authority.
Requests are handled free of charge, subject to rules by the Authority.
who: Businesses and bodies holding personal data
impl.when: The Act sets no start date. Certified 30 October 2025.

bills.about: Therapeutic use exemptions and anti-doping procedures for athletes.

impl.sum: Rewrites the rules on therapeutic use exemptions and the committee that grants them.

figs.l: minimum members of the exemption committee

changes: Repeals Part I of the 2013 Act.
An athlete with a medical condition may be allowed a prohibited substance if the rules' conditions are met.
Applications are made as soon as possible, and at least 30 days ahead for in-competition substances.
The committee has at least three medical members who must disclose conflicts of interest.
impl.when: The Act sets no start date. Certified 7 October 2025.

bills.about: Sets up the National Building Research Institute for landslide-prone and unstable areas.

impl.sum: Creates the National Building Research Institute as a statutory body for landslide and ground-stability research.
changes: Establishes the Institute as a body corporate.
It researches and surveys landslide-prone and geotechnically unstable areas.
It works to make construction in those areas disaster resilient, with technical help to authorities.
who: Builders and developers in landslide-prone areas
impl.when: The Act sets no start date. Certified 7 October 2025.

bills.about: Makes officials report suspected fraud found in audits to law enforcement.

impl.sum: Where an audit finds signs of fraud or corruption, the Auditor-General must have it reported to law enforcement.
changes: The Auditor-General notifies the Chief Accounting Officer, who must complain to a law enforcement authority at once.
If the allegation is against the Chief Accounting Officer, the Secretary to the Cabinet makes the complaint.
Those officers must report progress on the complaint to the Auditor-General.
Audit reports go to the Chief Accounting Officer, not the governing body, within a set time.
impl.when: The Act sets no start date. Certified 22 September 2025.

bills.about: Ends residences, allowances and pensions for former Presidents and their widows.

impl.sum: Repeals the 1986 Act; former Presidents and widows lose its residences, allowances and pensions.
changes: Repeals the Presidents' Entitlements Act, No. 4 of 1986.
Residences and monthly allowances for former Presidents and their widows stop.
Secretarial allowances, official transport and other facilities stop.
The monthly pension for widows of former Presidents stops.
impl.when: The Act sets no start date. Certified 10 September 2025.

bills.about: Creates a Gambling Regulatory Authority to license all gambling except state lotteries.

impl.sum: Creates a Gambling Regulatory Authority and makes all gambling, except state lotteries and social gambling, need a licence.

figs.l: minimum age to work in gambling

changes: Gambling needs a licence from the Authority's Director-General; premises must be registered.
Lotteries of the Development and National Lotteries Boards and social gambling are outside the Act.
Employing anyone under 21 in a gambling operation is an offence.
Repeals the Betting on Horse-Racing Ordinance, the Gaming Ordinance and the Casino Business (Regulation) Act of 2010.
impl.when: Most provisions start on a date set by the Minister by Gazette order. Certified 3 September 2025.

bills.about: Renames the Rubber Controller as Director-General and drops several old provisions.

impl.sum: Replaces the Rubber Controller with the Director-General of the Rubber Development Department.
changes: Every reference to the Controller becomes the Director-General of the Rubber Development Department.
Part VI is renamed Rubber Advisory Board.
Repeals sections 26, 36 to 39A and 50 of the Rubber Control Act.
impl.when: The Act sets no start date. Certified 22 August 2025.

bills.about: Brings Samurdhi community banks under the Auditor-General.

impl.sum: Makes the Auditor-General's audit rules apply to Samurdhi community-based banks and banking societies.
changes: New section 28A: Article 154 and the National Audit Act apply to Samurdhi community-based banks.
New section 35A: the same applies to Samurdhi community-based banking societies.
The Auditor-General's audit powers now reach these community-based banks.
impl.when: The Act sets no start date. Certified 22 August 2025.

bills.about: Changes to the 2024 electricity law on policy, the power market and restructuring.

impl.sum: Replaces the advisory council with a ministerial committee and renames the wholesale market the National Electricity Market.
changes: The National Electricity Advisory Council is replaced by a committee appointed by the Minister.
The Wholesale Electricity Market becomes the National Electricity Market.
The Act provides for a national electricity policy within the national energy policy.
Before restructuring orders, a transfer plan, a tariff policy and CEB generation and transmission plans must be ready.
impl.when: The Act sets no start date. Certified 18 August 2025.

bills.about: Electronic cheque presentation, a new dishonoured-cheque offence and updated rules.

impl.sum: Lets banks present cheques electronically and makes issuing a cheque that bounces without good reason an offence.

figs.l: maximum jail for a dishonoured cheque offence

changes: Banks may present a cheque by sending its image and payment data electronically.
Notice of dishonour may be given by fax or other electronic means.
Issuing a cheque that is dishonoured without legitimate reason can lead to a fine equal to the cheque or up to two years in jail.
Interest on bills is at the legal rate in force, not a fixed 9%.
References to Ceylon become Sri Lanka.
impl.when: The Act sets no start date. Certified 15 August 2025.

bills.about: Bans bearer shares and requires companies to record and report their beneficial owners.

impl.sum: Bans bearer shares and makes companies keep and file details of their beneficial owners.

figs.l: working days for shareholders to give details

changes: A company other than one limited by guarantee may have a single shareholder.
Companies may not issue bearer shares or share warrants to bearer.
Holders of existing bearer instruments must tell the company and convert them to registered shares within 60 days.
Companies must keep a register of beneficial owners and give the Registrar their names, addresses and ID numbers.
Shareholders must give these details within ten working days of buying or receiving shares.
impl.when: Most provisions start on a date set by the Minister by Gazette order. Certified 4 August 2025.

bills.about: Ends the 2016 budgetary relief allowance on 31 March 2025.

impl.sum: Limits the budgetary relief allowance under the 2016 Act to periods ending 31 March 2025.
changes: Both allowances under Act No. 4 of 2016 now end on 31 March 2025.
Passed alongside the minimum wage increase in Act No. 11 of 2025.
The change is treated as in force from 1 April 2025.
impl.when: Treated as in force from 1 April 2025.

bills.about: Ends the 2005 budgetary relief allowance on 31 March 2025.

impl.sum: Limits the budgetary relief allowance under the 2005 Act to August 2005 to March 2025.
changes: The allowance under Act No. 36 of 2005 now covers 1 August 2005 to 31 March 2025 only.
Passed alongside the minimum wage increase in Act No. 11 of 2025.
The change is treated as in force from 1 April 2025.
impl.when: Treated as in force from 1 April 2025.

bills.about: Raises the national minimum wage and folds in the budgetary relief allowances.

impl.sum: Raises the national minimum monthly wage to Rs. 27,000, then Rs. 30,000 from January 2026.
changes: Minimum monthly wage of Rs. 27,000 and daily wage of Rs. 1,080 from 1 April to 31 December 2025.
From 1 January 2026, Rs. 30,000 a month and Rs. 1,200 a day.
Budgetary relief allowances paid as at 31 March 2025 now count as part of the minimum wage.
who: Workers in any industry or service
impl.when: Treated as in force from 1 April 2025.

bills.about: Widens the Commission's role from inter-provincial buses to other road transport.

impl.sum: Extends the National Transport Commission from inter-provincial buses to office, school and three-wheeler services.
changes: The Act now covers road transportation, not only passenger transport by bus.
Inter-provincial office transport, school transport and three-wheeler services can come under the Commission.
The Minister can declare other inter-provincial road transport services.
The Commission sets standards to make road transport safe and comfortable.
impl.when: The Act sets no start date. Certified 19 June 2025.

bills.about: Lets Magistrates excuse suspects from attending court in person in special circumstances.

impl.sum: Lets a Magistrate excuse a suspect or accused from attending court in person in special circumstances.
changes: Attendance can be dispensed with for extending detention, bail hearings and other purposes.
The Attorney-General, the suspect or lawyer, or the police officer in charge can apply.
The Magistrate must be satisfied that one of the grounds in the Act applies.
impl.when: The Act sets no start date. Certified 18 June 2025.

bills.about: Repeals the 1957 Foreign Loans Act; existing loan agreements continue.

impl.sum: Repeals the Foreign Loans Act of 1957; existing loan agreements are treated as signed under the 2024 debt law.
changes: Repeals the Foreign Loans Act, No. 29 of 1957.
Loan agreements and guarantees signed under it count as signed under the Public Debt Management Act, No. 33 of 2024.
Orders made to give effect to those agreements stay in force until the obligations are met.
impl.when: The Act sets no start date. Certified 23 May 2025.

bills.about: Tracing, freezing and confiscating proceeds of crime, with a new management authority.

impl.sum: Sets up a system to investigate, restrain, forfeit and manage proceeds of crime, with a new authority.
changes: Provides for investigating, restraining, forfeiting and disposing of proceeds of crime.
Establishes the Proceeds of Crime Management Authority to protect and manage restrained property.
Provides for cooperation between agencies and with other countries.
who: People whose property is linked to crime
impl.when: The Act sets no start date. Certified 30 April 2025.

bills.about: VAT on digital services from abroad, registration of traders and electronic returns.

impl.sum: Brings foreign digital services into VAT from October 2025 and requires electronic VAT returns from July 2025.

figs.l: VAT on foreign digital services begins

changes: Services supplied by non-residents to people in Sri Lanka through electronic platforms are taxable from 1 October 2025.
Several deferred-payment and import concessions end for periods from 1 October 2025.
Anyone importing or exporting goods for commercial purposes must register for VAT.
Returns for periods from 1 July 2025 are filed electronically, with exceptions allowed.
Free or subsidised staff meals and transport are valued at zero from January 2024.
impl.when: Certified 11 April 2025. One change is treated as in force from 1 January 2024; others from July and October 2025.

bills.about: The 2025 Budget: government spending and borrowing for the year.

impl.sum: Authorises Rs. 4,218.2 billion of spending in 2025 and caps borrowing at Rs. 4,000 billion.
changes: Sets spending for every ministry and department for 2025.
Limits loans raised during or outstanding at the end of 2025 to Rs. 4,000 billion.
Sets limits for advance account activities.
Loan details go in the final budget position report to Parliament.
impl.when: Covers 1 January to 31 December 2025.

bills.about: New personal income tax bands and rates from April 2025.

impl.sum: New income tax bands from April 2025, personal relief of Rs. 1.8 million and 15% on foreign-currency service income.

figs.l: rate on betting, liquor and tobacco profits

changes: Individuals pay 6% on the first Rs. 1 million of taxable income, rising in bands to 36% above Rs. 2.5 million.
Personal relief is Rs. 1,800,000 a year from 1 April 2025.
Service income earned in foreign currency and remitted through a bank is taxed at no more than 15%.
Profits from betting and gaming, liquor and tobacco are taxed at 45%.
Withholding on interest or discount rises from 5% to 10%.
Refunds for years from April 2024 must be claimed within 30 months of the year's end.
impl.when: 1 April 2025.

bills.about: Cancels 2023 nominations and calls fresh local authority elections.

impl.sum: Voids nominations for the postponed 2023 local elections and requires fresh nominations within three months.

figs.l: date of the elections not held

changes: Nomination papers filed for the local authority elections due on 9 March 2023 have no effect.
The earlier notices of nomination are revoked.
Candidate deposits are refunded on production of the receipt.
The Election Commission must publish fresh nomination notices within three months.
impl.when: The Act sets no start date. Certified 17 February 2025.

bills.about: Port City pay in foreign currency, income tax exemptions and offshore banking rules.

impl.sum: Gives three years of income tax exemption to existing Port City businesses' staff and sets offshore banking rules.
changes: Businesses approved before the Act may employ residents or non-residents and pay them in foreign currency.
For three years, their employees' employment income is exempt from income tax.
Employees of businesses approved after the Act are liable to income tax.
The Commission licenses offshore banking in the Port City; the Central Bank regulates it to international standards.
No fee, including a land use fee, may be charged before a licence and registration are issued.
impl.when: The Act sets no start date. Certified 20 January 2026.

bills.about: Bans corporal punishment of children and raises penalties for hurting a child.
Stops landlords from cutting utilities or forcing out lawful occupants.
Repeals the Rent Act of 1972, with one year of protection for existing tenants.
Five-year exemption from the cellular tower levy for new towers.
Extends the telecommunication levy to service providers and lets operators deduct bad debts.
